Name: Dynamic Map Tiles
Author: aedenthorn
Description:
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/33900][b][size=5]Dynamic Map Tiles Extended is out![/size]

It is a complete rewrite of this mod thanks to MindMeltMax, with lots of new functionality and better syntax. The old mod here will no longer be updated. Click here to download the new one instead![/b][/url] 


[b][size=4]Old mod description:[/size][/b]


This mod is a framework that lets you easily create dynamic game mechanics simply by assigning tile properties to individual map tiles.

Functionality currently includes:

[list]
[*]changing the tile index of one or more tiles (works with animated tiles)
[*]changing tile properties of one or more tiles
[*]allowing a tile to be destroyed by bombs
[*]causing an explosion
[*]allowing a tile to be pushed
[*]playing a sound
[*]playing a temporary sprite animation
[*]instantly teleporting a farmer to anywhere on the map
[*]giving an item
[*]taking the held object
[*]spawning a chest
[*]showing a message
[*]playing a custom event string
[*]setting a mail flag
[*]invalidating an asset
[*]changing the music
[*]healing or damaging a farmer's health or stamina all at once or over time
[*]applying a buff to a farmer
[*]modifying a farmer's movement speed while on a tile
[*]moving a farmer in a direction while on a tile
[*]making a farmer emote
[*]making a tile slippery
[/list]

Here's two videos showing examples of some of the above:

[youtube]ug6m_gR-SpI[/youtube]

[youtube]96frrEfuSHs[/youtube]


An example of a mod that uses this framework is [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/14597]Chest Room for Additional Mine Maps[/url].


[b][size=5]Setting Tile Properties[/size][/b]

The simplest way to implement this mod's features is using Content Patcher to modify map tile properties. E.g.:

[code]﻿{
    "Format": "1.23.0",
    "Changes": [
        {
            "Action": "EditMap",
            "Target": "Maps/Farm",
            "MapTiles": [
                {
                    "Position": { "X": 72, "Y": 15 },
                    "Layer": "Back",
                    "SetProperties": {
                        "DMT/changeIndexOn": "69"
                    }
                }
            ]
        },
    ]
}
[/code]
This changes the tile index of 72,15 on the Farm to 69 when the farmer steps on it.

This mod also offers a means of adding tile properties automatically using Content Patcher:

[code]{
"Format": "1.23.0",
"Changes": [
{
"Action": "EditData",
"Target": "aedenthorn.DynamicMapTiles/dictionary",
"Entries": {
"aedenthorn.IceTiles": {
"locations": [
"Forest"
],
"layers": [
"Back"
],
"tileSheets": [
"fest"
],
"tileSheetPaths": [
"Festivals"
],
﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿"indexes": [
226,
227
],
"rectangles": [
{
"X": 0,
"Y": 0,
"Width": 100,
"Height": 100,
}
],
"properties": {
"DMT/slippery": "0.25"
}
}
}
}
]
}
[/code]
This example sets the property [b]DMT/slippery[/b] to [b]0.25[/b] on all tiles that fit the parameters above (in Forest, on Back layer, with indexes 226 and 227 on tilesheet "fest" with path containing "Festivals", with x and y coordinates within the given rectangle). Any parameter can be omitted if not used.


[size=5][b]Key Triggering
[/b][/size]

[b][size=4]Trigger Once[/size]

[/b]Any of the property keys below can be suffixed with [b]Once[/b] to have the property be removed once it has been triggered once.


[b][size=4]Conditional Triggers[/size]
[/b]
Both ordinary keys and those with the [b]Once [/b]suffix can then take one of the following suffixes to determine how they are triggered:

[list]
[*][b]Explode[/b] - triggered when the tile is destroyed by an explosion (tiles that have the [b]DMT/explode[/b] key)
[*][b]Push[/b] - triggered when the tile is pushed
[*][b]Pushed[/b] - triggered once a tile has finished being pushed
[*][b]On[/b] - triggered when the farmer steps on the tile (Back tiles only)
[*][b]Off[/b] - triggered when the farmer steps off the tile (Back tiles only)
[/list]
Some keys are triggered in other ways and do not require a suffix.


[b][size=4]Tool Triggers[/size][/b]

Most keys can be triggered when using a tool on a tile, by adding the class name of a tool (not the language specific display name) as a suffix. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/soundOnceWateringCan": "steam"[/b]

will trigger when one waters the tile with a watering can.

Tool class names in the vanilla code are:

[list]
[*][b]MagnifyingGlass[/b]
[*][b]Shears[/b]
[*][b]MilkPail[/b]
[*][b]Axe[/b]
[*][b]Wand[/b]
[*][b]Hoe[/b]
[*][b]FishingRod[/b]
[*][b]MeleeWeapon[/b]
[*][b]Pan[/b]
[*][b]Pickaxe[/b]
[*][b]WateringCan[/b]
[*][b]Slingshot[/b]
[*][b]GenericTool[/b]
[/list]

[b][size=4]Object Triggers[/size][/b]

Most keys can be triggered when acting on a tile while holding a specific object by adding "[b]Object[/b]" plus either the held object's index number or its name (not display name). E.g.:

[b]"DMT/soundObjectPrismatic Shard": "yoba"[/b]

To have the object be removed on trigger, combine this with the [b]DMT/take[/b] key. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/takeObjectPrismatic Shard": ""[/b] - this will take the player's active object if the tile is acted on while holding a Prismatic Shard.


[b][size=4]Action Triggers[/size][/b]

Most keys can be triggered simply by acting on the tile by adding "[b]Action[/b]" to the end of the key. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/soundAction": "yoba"[/b]


[b][size=4]SMAPI C# Triggers[/size][/b]

To trigger any tile's keys from another C# mod, you can use SMAPI's mod API interface. The API interface for this mod is:

[code]﻿    public interface IDynamicMapTilesApi
    {
        public bool TriggerActions(List<Layer> layers, Farmer farmer, Point tilePos, List<string> suffixes);
    }
[/code]
[b]suffixes[/b] should be a list of all the kinds of trigger outlined above that you want to trigger.


[b][size=5]Key List[/size][/b]

All possible keys are explained in detail below, organized as follows:

[list]
[*][size=4][b]Buffs[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Cache Invalidation[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Emotes[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Events[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Explosions[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Health and Stamina[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Items & Chests[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Mail[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Messages[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Music[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Pushing[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Sound[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Speed & Movement[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Temporary Sprite Animations[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Teleportation[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Tile Indexes[/b][/size]
[*][size=4][b]Tile Properties[/b][/size]
[/list]

[size=5][b]Buffs[/b]
[/size]
[b]DMT/buff

[/b]The above key can be used to add a buff/debuff to the player. The value should be the integer index of the buff/debuff. Buff indexes are as follows:

[list]
[*]6 Full
[*]7 Quenched
[*]12 Burnt
[*]13 Slimed
[*]14 Jinxed
[*]17 Tipsy
[*]18 Spooked
[*]19 Frozen
[*]20 Warrior Energy
[*]21 Yoba's Blessing
[*]22 Adrenaline Rush
[*]23 Oil of Garlic
[*]24 Monster Musk
[*]25 Nauseous
[*]26 Darkness
[*]27 Weakness
[*]28 Squid Ink Ravioli
[/list]
E.g.:

[b]"DMT/buffOn"[/b]: "13" - triggers the slimed buff when stepping on the tile. 


[b][size=5]Cache Invalidation[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/invalidate[/b]

You can trigger the invalidation of cached game assets using [b]DMT/invalidate[/b]. The value should be a list of asset paths separated by the pipe symbol "|".


[b][size=5]Emotes[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/emote[/b]

This key causes a farmer to emote. The value should be the integer index of the specific emote. Emote indexes are:

[list]
[*]4 empty can
[*]8 question mark
[*]12 angry
[*]16 exclamation
[*]20 heart
[*]24 sleep
[*]28 sad
[*]32 happy
[*]36 x
[*]40 pause
[*]44 not used
[*]48 not used
[*]52 videogame
[*]56 music note
[*]60 blush
[/list]

[b][size=5]Events[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/event
[/b]
Use the above key to trigger a custom event. See [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Event_data]Modding:Event data[/url] on the wiki. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/eventOn": "playful/20 57/Harvey 25 57 3/skippable/pause 200/speak Harvey \"Hey, why are you stepping there, @?\"/pause 500/end"[/b]


[b][size=5]Explosions[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/explode
[/b][b]DMT/explosion
[/b]
Tiles can be marked as explodable by adding the property [b]DMT/explode[/b] to the tile. The tile will be removed when affected by a bomb. Tiles on different layers will be checked individually.

The value of the key should be left blank "" unless you want the mod to set a mail flag for the player - then set the value to the mail id to be sent. This can be useful for making the explosion persistent, as Content Patcher can then check for the flag and remove the tile on next load.

You can trigger other properties on explode by adding [b]"Explode"[/b] to the end of the property key; tiles with properties ending with [b]Explode[/b] will be triggered when [b]DMT/explode[/b] is triggered on that tile. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/explode": "",
[b]"DMT/soundExplode": "yoba"[/b][/b]

Tiles can trigger an explosion somewhere in the map when stepped on by adding the property [b]DMT/explosion[/b]. The value of the property should be the following:

[b]<TileX> <TileY> <radius> <damagesFarmer(true or false)> <damageAmount> [/b]

e.g.:

[b]"DMT/explosionOnceOn": "17 26 8 false -1"[/b]


[size=5][b]Health and Stamina[/b][/size]

[b]DMT/health
DMT/stamina
DMT/healthPerSecond
DMT/staminaPerSecond[/b]

These keys can be used to affect the player health and stamina all at once or when standing on a tile over time (the PerSecond keys should be used on the "Back" layer only and will be triggered while standing on the tile; they should not take a suffix).

The property value should be a positive or negative integer.


[b][size=5]Items & Chests
[/size][/b]
[b]DMT/give
[b]DMT/chest
[/b]DMT/take

[size=4]Give[/size]

[/b]To give the player an item, use the key [b]DMT/give[/b]. The item will be held up by the farmer and placed in their inventory (or on the ground if full).

For ordinary objects, the value should be either the index in ObjectInformation or the name of the object in ObjectInformation.

To give other types of items, use [b]<ItemType>/<IndexOrName>[/b]. The following types are supported:

[list]
[*]Hat
[*]Clothing
[*]Craftable
[*]Furniture
[*]Weapon
[*]Money
[/list]
E.g.:

[b]"DMT/giveOn": "Clothing/Skull Shirt"[/b]

[b][size=4]Chest[/size][/b]

To spawn a chest somewhere in the map, use [b]DMT/chest[/b]. The syntax is:

[b]<TileX> <TileY>=<item1> <item2>...
[/b]
Item syntax is the same as for [b]DMT/give[/b] except you can specify an amount using <item>,<amount> E.g.:

[b]"DMT/chestOn": "8 26=Money/1000 [b]Clothing/Skull Shirt [/b]378,10"[/b] - this spawns a chest with 1000 coins, a skull shirt, and 10 copper ore.

[b][size=4]Take[/size][/b]

To take one of the player's held item use [b]DMT/take[/b]. If the value is empty, the item will be taken no matter what it is. If the value is either a specific object index or name, it will only take if the held item index or name matches. This is useful for combining with [b]Object<nameOrIndex>[/b] suffixed triggers so that the item is consumed and something else happens as a result.


[b][size=5]Mail[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/mail
DMT/mailbox

[/b]Use the above keys to send mail. The value is the id for the mail to be sent.

The first key will simply set a mail flag as having been received. The second key will actually put the mail with that id into the mailbox. The first is useful for setting flags to tell Content Patcher mods that the tile has been stepped on before.


[b][size=5]Messages[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/message

[/b]Use the above key to show a  HUD message.


[b][size=5]Music
[/size][/b]
[b]DMT/music[/b]

Use the above key to change the currently playing music track. The value should be the id of a music track in the game.


[b][size=5]Pushing[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/push
[b]DMT/pushAlso[/b]
DMT/pushOthers
[b]DMT/pushable[/b]
[/b]
Only tiles on the Buildings layer can use the property [b]DMT/push[/b], which lets you push them by walking into them. The value of the property should be a comma-separated list of all tiles (X Y) that the tile is pushable to. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/push": "1 1,1 2,2 1,2 2"[/b] - this tile can be pushed to any of the four tiles in the list.

You can trigger pushing other tiles when a tile is pushed using [b]DMT/pushAlso[/b]. The format for [b]DMT/[/b][b]pushAlso[/b] value is:

[b]<tile1layer> <tile1xOffset> <tile1yOffset>,<tile2layer> <tile2xOffset> <tile2yOffset>...
[/b]
E.g.:

[b]"DMT/[b]pushAlso[/b]": "Buildings -1 0,Front -1 -1,Front 0 -1"[/b] - pushes three other tiles when this tile is pushed, with x y tile positions relative to this tile.

Tiles that are included in another tile's [b]pushAlso [/b]list should have the property [b]"DMT/pushable"[/b] added to them if there is a concern with different sets of pushable tiles colliding and erasing each other. Tiles without this property will be overridden by tiles pushed into their position. 

You can trigger other properties on push by adding [b]"Push"[/b] to the end of the property key; exploded tiles with properties ending with [b]Push[/b] will be triggered when [b]DMT/push[/b] is triggered on that tile. E.g.:

[b][b]"DMT/soundPush": "furnace"[/b][/b]

You can trigger other properties when a tile is finished being pushed by adding [b]"Pushed"[/b] to the end of the property key; exploded tiles with properties ending with [b]Pushed[/b] will be triggered when a tile being push reaches its destination tile. E.g.:

[b][b]"DMT/soundPushed": "yoba"[/b][/b]

[b]Push[/b] and [b]Pushed[/b] suffixes can also be added to tiles on other layers, so that when you push a tile onto or off of another tile it triggers the properties on that tile. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/explosionOncePushed": "17 26 8 false -1"[/b] - this can be added to a tile on the Back layer so that when a tile on the Buildings layer is pushed onto it, it triggers an explosion once. [b]Push[/b] suffix will be triggered on tiles when a tile is pushed off of them instead.

To trigger the pushing of tiles other than the triggering tile use [b]DMT/pushOthers[/b]. This key takes a list of [b]Layer X Y[/b] values separated by commas like [b]pushAlso[/b]. Note that each tile pushed this way will trigger its own [b]pushAlso [/b]key, so there is no need to push all joined tiles with this trigger.


[b][size=5]Sound[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/sound
[/b]
To play a sound, use one of the above keys. The value should be a valid vanilla sound key (see [url=https://stardewvalleywiki.com/Modding:Audio]Modding:Audio[/url]﻿ on the wiki).

Playing a sound once means the property will be removed once the sound has been played. This is not persistent (the sound will be able to play again if the map is reloaded). Use mail flags and Content Patcher for persistence.


[b][size=5]Speed & Movement
[/size][/b]
[b]DMT/speed
DMT/move
[b]DMT/slippery[/b]

[/b]The speed key can be used to affect the player's movement speed while moving over a tile. The value should be the decimal multiplier (1 is no change, 0.5 is half speed, etc.).

The move key can be used to apply directional velocity while on a tile. The value should be decimal x and y values separated by a space. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/move": "2.5 0"[/b] - applies 2.5x velocity towards the right while on the tile with this property.

The slippery key can be used to make tiles slippery. The value should be a decimal, which seems to be equivalent to a fraction of the player's ordinary move speed. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/slippery": "0.25"[/b] - this simulates ordinary ice tiles


[b][size=5]Temporary Sprite Animations[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/animation[/b]

Animations are complex things - they are not difficult to code, just have many possible parameters. I've added two options for triggering animations, one with 16 parameters and one with 29 (!) parameters. Parameters should be separated by commas. For multiple animations, separate them using the pipe symbol "[b]|[/b]".

[b][size=4]Indexed Animations[/size][/b]

Indexed animations use the game's built in animations data sheet. If you want to trigger any of those, look at the [b]TileSheets/animations[/b] file. The parameters should be:

[b][int rowInAnimationTexture],[int position.X],[int position.Y],[int color.R],[int color.G],[int color.B],[int color.A],[int animationLength],[bool flipped],[float animationInterval],[int numberOfLoops],[int sourceRectWidth],[float layerDepth], [int sourceRectHeight],[int delay],[int ID]
[/b]

[b][size=4]Custom Animations[/size][/b]

For animations using custom textures, use the following parameters:

[b][string textureName],[int sourceRect.X],[int sourceRect.Y],[int sourceRect.Width],[int sourceRect.Height],[float animationInterval],[int animationLength],[int numberOfLoops],[int position.X],[int position.Y],[bool flicker],[bool flipped],[float layerDepth],[float alphaFade],[int color.R],[int color.G],[int color.B],[int color.A],[float scale],[float scaleChange],[float rotation],[float rotationChange],[bool local],[float motion.X],[float motion.Y],[float acceleration.X],[float acceleration.Y],[int delayBeforeAnimationStart],[int ID][/b]


So, here's an attempt at recreating the steam on watering a lava tile:

[b]"DMT/animationOnceWateringCan": "LooseSprites\\Cursors,372,1956,10,10,99999,1,0,{{Random:{{Range:1152,1216}}|key=a1}},{{Random:{{Range:768,832}}|key=a6}},false,false,-1,0.007,255,255,255,255,4,0.02,0,0.012,false,0,0,0,0,35,4205|LooseSprites\\Cursors,372,1956,10,10,99999,1,0,{{Random:{{Range:1152,1216}}|key=a2}},{{Random:{{Range:768,832}}|key=a7}},false,false,-1,0.007,255,255,255,255,4,0.02,0,0.012,false,0,0,0,0,35,4206|LooseSprites\\Cursors,372,1956,10,10,99999,1,0,{{Random:{{Range:1152,1216}}|key=a3}},{{Random:{{Range:768,832}}|key=a8}},false,false,-1,0.007,255,255,255,255,4,0.02,0,0.012,false,0,0,0,0,35,4207|LooseSprites\\Cursors,372,1956,10,10,99999,1,0,{{Random:{{Range:1152,1216}}|key=a4}},{{Random:{{Range:768,832}}|key=a9}},false,false,-1,0.007,255,255,255,255,4,0.02,0,0.012,false,0,0,0,0,35,4208|LooseSprites\\Cursors,372,1956,10,10,99999,1,0,{{Random:{{Range:1152,1216}}|key=a5}},{{Random:{{Range:768,832}}|key=a10}},false,false,-1,0.007,255,255,255,255,4,0.02,0,0.012,false,0,0,0,0,35,4209"[/b]

This creates five different animations using Content Patcher randomization for position.


[b][size=5]Teleportation
[/size][/b]
[b]DMT/teleport[/b]
[b]DMT/teleportTile[/b]

To instantly teleport anywhere on the current map when stepping on a tile, use the above key.  For the first key, the value should be the exact x y coordinates to teleport to. For the second key, use the tile x y coordinates instead. E.g.:

[b]"DMT/teleportTileOn": "10 10"[/b] and [b]"DMT/teleportOn": "640 640"[/b] - both teleport the player to the tile 10,10 when stepping on the tile with this property. With the second key you can of course use non-multiples of 64 for precise teleportation (Heisenberg compensator sold seperately).


[b][size=5]Tile Indexes
[/size][/b]
[b]DMT/changeIndex[/b]
[b]DMT/changeMultipleIndex[/b]


[size=4][b][b]DMT/changeIndex[/b][/b]
[/size]
To change the tile index to another index on the same tile sheet, the value should be the new integer index. e.g:

[b]"[b]DMT/changeIndexOn[/b]": "69"[/b]

To change to a different tile sheet, use the following syntax:

[b]tileSheetName/index[/b]

e.g.:

[b]"DMT/changeIndexOn": "Landscape/69"[/b] - will change the tile to use index [b]69[/b] on the [b]Landscape[/b] tile sheet when the farmer steps on it.

For animated tiles, use the following syntaxes instead:

[b]staticIndex1 [/b][b]staticIndex2 [/b][b]staticIndex3,duration

[/b]or

[b]tileSheetName/staticIndex1 [b]tileSheetName/[/b][/b][b]staticIndex2 [b]tileSheetName/[/b][/b][b]staticIndex3,duration

[/b]e.g.:

[b][b]"[b]DMT/changeIndexOn[/b]": "[/b]Landscape/67 Landscape/68 [/b][b]Landscape/69,100"[/b] - will change the tile to an animated tile using three static tile indexes from the Landscape tile sheet, 100ms per tile

To remove a tile, leave the entire value blank [b]""[/b].


[b][size=4]DMT/changeMultipleIndex[/size]
[/b]
The syntax is similar to that above. Info for each tile being changed is separated by the pipe symbol "[b]|[/b]":

[b]<tileInfo1>|<tileInfo2>[/b]

Each tile info is separated into two parts by an equals sign:

[b]<layerXY>=<indexDuration>

[/b]The part before the equals sign is separated by spaces, containing the layer name, x coordinate, and y coordinate. The part after the equals sign is the same as the section on changing single tiles above (either [b]idx[/b] or [b]idx1 idx2 idx3,duration[/b]). E.g.:

[b]"DMT/changeMultipleIndexOn": "Back 5 10=150|Buildings 6 9=Landscape/67 Landscape/68 Landscape/69,100"[/b] - changes one back tile (5,10) to a static tile and one building tile (6,9) to an animated tile using the data given, when the farmer steps on the tile with this property.

To remove a tile, just don't put anything after the equals sign.


[b][size=5]Tile Properties[/size][/b]

[b]DMT/changeProperties
DMT/changeMultipleProperties
[/b]
Similar to the previous section, use these keys for changing the current tile properties, or changing multiple tiles' properties.

For the current tile's properties:

Properties are split by the pipe symbol [b]"|"[/b]. Each property has a key and value:

[b]prop1key=prop1value|prop2key=prop2value

[/b]E.g.:

[b]"DMT/changePropertiesOn": "Action=Crib|Passable=T"

[/b]To remove a property, omit the equal sign and the value:

[b]"DMT/changePropertiesOn": "Action|Passable"[/b] - removes both these properties from the stepped on tile.


For multiple tile properties, separate tile info using the pipe sign as before, [b]"|"[/b]. The info for each tile is almost the same as above, except it contains the tile info as well, separated using commas (because idk if the key might have spaces in it):

[b]tile1layer,tile1x,tile1y,prop1key=prop1value|tile2layer,tile2x,tile2y,prop2key=prop2value

[/b]E.g.:

[b]"DMT/changeMultiplePropertiesOff": "Buildings,6,9,[b]Action=Crib|[b]Back,9,6,[/b]Passable=T[/b]"[/b] - sets two different properties on two different tiles on two different layers.

To remove a property, just don't put anything after the equals sign.
